newsitem.title: NIGERIA: World Bank plans seminar on investing in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans seminar on investing in Nigeria.

text.p: Nigeria's finance minister Anthony Ani said on Monday that the World Bank planned to stage a seminar next month on investing in Nigeria.
"The World Bank has scheduled a seminar titled: 'Investing in Nigeria' for November 1 in Washington," Ani told a seminar in Lagos on attracting foreign investment into the country.
"It is the first time the World Bank would organise such a workshop on Nigeria, which means they are now happy with our economic policies," he added.

The World Bank and the private sector has long been urging Nigeria to revive its economy, the biggest in Sub-Saharan Africa, by privatising key sectors such as electricity, petroleum and telecommunications.

The military government has introduced key measures in the last 18 months like free trading in the naira, allowing full repatriation of profits and removed curbs on interest rates to encourage foreign investors.

Ani earlier told the Lagos seminar that Nigeria was seriously considering selling its oil joint ventures and privatising its refineries. The military government has already announced that it will privatise the National Electric Power Authority and Nigerian Telecommunications next year.

"Our relationship has been improving day by day now, compared to say sometime in 1994. The Nigerian government is now gradually seeing reason with our ideas," Tom Hutcheson, the World Bank's resident economist told the Lagos seminar, but added that more positive economic policies were expected.
Ani said about 130 representatives of the World Bank will be present at the Washington seminar to be attended by private businessmen from around the world.
